 Inside the numbers behind another woeful Syracuse women’s soccer campaign
 Syracuse women’s soccer players react to a play in the team’s 2-0 loss to Cal on Nov. 5. SU finished the season 4-11-2 and missed the postseason for the 14th straight year.
 Peter Hua Radosh | Asst. Digital Editor 
 By
 Spencer Brod 
 Asst. Sports Editor
 November 10, 2026

 Post

 Copy link 
 Get the latest Syracuse news delivered right to your inbox. 
 Subscribe to our newsletter here . 
 Nicky Thrasher Adams is used to having her Novembers free by now.
 For the 14th straight season, Syracuse women’s soccer missed the postseason. SU went 4-11-2 overall and 1-9-0 in Atlantic Coast Conference play in 2026. Since Adams became the Orange’s head coach in 2019, they haven’t won more than one ACC game in a season. 
 Syracuse looked promising to start 2026, going 3-0-1 with wins over Holy Cross , Northwestern and Princeton . SU’s offense scored three goals against the Crusaders and Tigers, giving it hope entering conference play. 
 But that hope was short-lived. Across their final three nonconference games and 10 ACC contests, the Orange were outscored 26-5. Syracuse most notably lost 6-1 to then-No. 13 Louisville on Oct. 23, allowing a program-record six goals in the first half. 
 Now that the season has concluded, here are four stats that defined SU’s (4-11-2, 1-9-0 ACC) 2026 campaign: 
 Maya Naimoli’s 72 saves 
 Entering 2026, Syracuse had one pressing question: Who would replace Shea Vanderbosch?
 Vanderbosch, SU’s goalie from 2022-25, finished with a program-best 380 saves and led the ACC in total saves and saves per game from 2023-25. But her graduation left SU with a gap to fill. 
 Enter Maya Naimoli . 
 Naimoli, who transferred to SU after stints with Ohio State and Youngstown State, was the Orange’s saving grace in an otherwise lost season. She led the ACC with 72 saves, ranked second with 4.50 saves per game and recorded four clean sheets. 
 The redshirt junior cemented herself as Syracuse’s No. 1 goalie in her first game, a draw against Villanova where she made four second-half saves. Ten days later against Princeton , she saved five shots against a fast-paced Tigers attack. She earned ACC Goalkeeper of the Week for the performance, SU’s first weekly honor since 2016.
 After allowing two goals in her ACC debut against Boston College on Sept. 13, Naimoli rebounded with five saves at Clemson on Sept. 17 and five more against Virginia Tech on Sept. 20. Naimoli then kicked it into high gear, notching eight saves against Pitt on Sept. 24 and then-No. 15 Virginia on Oct. 3. 
 Perhaps Naimoli’s most impressive showing came against NC State on Oct. 15. Despite Syracuse’s 1-0 loss, Naimoli held the Wolfpack’s offense — which ended the season fourth in the ACC with 40 goals — to just one score on six shots on goal. 
 A key element of Naimoli’s success was rebounding from poor performances, and she did so against Miami on Oct. 29. After allowing six goals on six shots on goal against Louisville on Oct. 23, she notched eight saves on 10 shots on goal against the Hurricanes. 
 Replacing Vanderbosch was a tall task, but SU found its answer in 2026. 
 4 ACC goals 
 Naimoli did all she could to keep Syracuse in games, but it often wasn’t enough. That’s because SU’s offense was pitiful in ACC play. Again. 
 In 2024 and 2025, the Orange scored five goals in 10 games, bottom-two marks in the conference or tied for it in both years. This season, Syracuse’s four goals in 10 ACC contests ranked last, and it wasn’t particularly close. Miami was second-to-last with nine. 
 After SU’s top 2025 scorers Ashley Rauch and Mia Klammer departed, Adams added Michigan transfer Vickie Jones and UConn’s Farrah Stephens-Martin , among others, to fill the void. Jones and Stephens-Martin combined for four goals in nonconference play but just one in 10 ACC games. 
 Ana Rodriguez | Design Editor 
 Syracuse also didn’t get much offensive production from Moo Galbus, Anna Croyle and Gabby Wisbeck , as the three everyday starters combined for just one ACC goal — a penalty kick from Wisbeck against Miami. 
 More alarmingly, SU couldn’t match its opponents in shots . Against Clemson, Syracuse was outshot 21-5. Against Virginia, it was outshot 23-1 and didn’t record a shot on goal for the first time since September 2021. Even in their 2-1 win over Pitt, the Orange were outshot 26-15. 
 SU’s 80 ACC shots tied for second-to-last with California and just ahead of Miami’s 75. Its 32 shots on goal also only ranked ahead of the Hurricanes. Even when Syracuse had shots on goal, they were often weak and easily saved. 
 Syracuse hasn’t had to worry about its goalie in five years. But it’s had to worry about its offense against ACC opponents every year under Adams. 
 Abby Incorvaia’s 9 points
 Syracuse’s offense was woeful in 2026. Little evidence refutes that. But one bright spot was Abby Incorvaia. 
 Incorvaia’s breakout sophomore season came out of nowhere. Despite playing in all 18 games in 2025, she was 16th on SU with 272 total minutes. She had four shots on goal but didn’t score or record any assists. 
 Incorvaia didn’t start SU’s season opener but started its next two games against Holy Cross and Northwestern. With Syracuse tied 0-0 late against the Wildcats, she buried a 90th-minute penalty kick into the top-left corner to win the game.
 Three days later against Princeton, she scored in the 59th minute to put SU up 2-0. Twenty-one seconds later, she assisted Stephens-Martin’s goal. 
 Against Pitt, Incorvaia thought she scored 100 seconds into the game, but the goal was negated due to an offside call. But she wasn’t deterred , scoring two minutes later to give SU an early 1-0 lead. She then assisted Stephens-Martin’s 88th-minute game-winner, spearheading the Orange’s first home ACC win since 2022. 
 SU hasn’t had many offensive building blocks recently, but Incorvaia should be the centerpiece of Syracuse’s attack moving forward.
 0 freshman points 
 Seven goals for Boston College’s Addy Kalaw. Four goals for Miami’s Zoie Fontenot. Six assists for SMU’s Julianne Richter. 
 What do those players all have in common? They’re freshmen.
 Syracuse had six freshmen on its roster this season, but they rarely made an impact, combining for zero points. Sarah Weisberg’s 280 minutes were the most among SU’s freshmen but ranked 17th on the Orange.
 WHAT YOU SHOULD READ NEXT 
 Syracuse women’s soccer’s ACC woes persist in season-ending loss to Cal
 Syracuse women’s soccer’s 2-0 defeat to Cal on Thursday capped another disappointing Atlantic Coast Conference campaign. SU finished last in the conference for the sixth time, extending its 14-year postseason drought.
 Lauren Christy scored twice in Syracuse’s preseason exhibition win over Mercyhurst but started just two regular season games. SU’s other first-year offensive players Oceane Blouin and Mady Wright didn’t play at all. 
 Incorvaia’s presence is a positive, but she seems to be the only underclassman the Orange attack can build around. SU’s freshmen could play a larger role as sophomores, but their 2026 campaigns weren’t an encouraging first step.
